newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Trade in Zimbabwean stocks seen losing steam.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Zimbabwean stocks seen losing steam.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares opened the week active but easier with market analysts predicting trade would slow down in the coming week as buyers and sellers failed to reach a compromise on prices.
"I don't think we'll be seeing much trade this week. No one seems willing to change their prices. Both buyers and sellers are just pegging their prices and sitting on them," one broker said.
The brokers however said trade was likely to pick up in March when investors rushed to stake their claims on some of the new listings expected on the exchange.
"Everyone is just waiting for the new issues and we should see more activity on the market then," said one.

On Monday, the 57-counter industrial index shed 11.5 points to close at 10,264.62 pressured down mainly by a 70 cent loss in hotel giant Meikles at 2,030, while Zimbabwe Alloys shed 40 cents to 750 and financial group Finhold eased 20 cents to 830.
Minings continued lifeless, with most stocks trading unchanged while a 200 cent drop to 2,400 in gold producer Rio Tinto pushed the seven-share index 19.44 ponts down to 1,020.62.
